result.title: Mitigating Spatial Blindness in Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Analysis
result.summary: Whole-slide multiple instance learning can predict diagnostic and prognostic labels from tissue composition while making limited use of spatial organization. Providing coordinates or a graph does not establish that a trained predictor uses tissue neighborhoods. We examine this gap as spatial blindness and hypothesize that early composition learning can weaken supervision of a spatial pathway. We introduce ResTopoMIL, which freezes a learned composition predictor before training a graph residual with a coordinate-reassignment separation loss. Permutation and information analyses distinguish architectural symmetry, available spatial information and the proposed optimization mechanism. On a controlled spatial task, staged training achieved an AUC of 0.987, compared with 0.684 for the same jointly trained architecture. Performance remained high on a composition-only task. Across four WSI classification and five survival benchmarks, ResTopoMIL improved mean primary performance on eight tasks; four improvements remained significant after Holm-adjusted patient-cluster tests. Coordinate-free residual controls recovered some of the gains, while neighborhood destruction reduced performance close to the composition anchor. Neighborhood-preserving transformations and anatomy-stratified perturbations further characterized this dependence. These results support fixing a composition reference as a practical intervention for learning spatial corrections, while retaining additional appearance capacity as a contributing explanation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究全切片图像多示例学习中的「空间盲」问题，提出 ResTopoMIL：先冻结已学好的组织构成预测器，再训练图残差分支并配合坐标重分配分离损失，以检验模型是否真正利用空间邻域信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分阶段冻结与辅助分支分离损失，可能为 LVR 中防止答案绕过 latent 视觉状态、确保空间或视觉通路获得有效监督提供可核查的训练线索，但跨域迁移尚未验证。
